column7: Short description / role
Provides file‑system routing, server‑side rendering, static generation, API routes and automatic optimisation for React apps.
Declarative component model; the basis for all UI pieces (Hero, dark‑mode toggle, etc.).
Supplies low‑level utility classes (bg-gray-900, flex, dark:) that you compose directly in markup.
A large banner that accepts title, subtitle, and CTA props; can also fetch and display metrics.
Adds/removes a class="dark" on <html> (or <body>) to switch Tailwind’s dark: variants.
High‑performance API framework that auto‑generates OpenAPI docs and validates request data via type hints.
Zero‑config, single‑file DB; perfect for prototyping or low‑traffic services.
GET /api/metrics returns JSON {visits, signups, revenue} pulled from SQLite.
Numbers that represent site activity; produced by the back‑end and consumed by the front‑end.
Performs the GET request to /api/metrics and parses the JSON response.
Runs side‑effects (e.g., data fetching) after a component mounts or when dependencies change.
Holds mutable component state (e.g., the fetched metrics) and triggers re‑render on change.
Allows a browser page on a different origin to call the API; not needed when both live under the same domain.
Detects a Next.js project, builds it, and serves via a global CDN; API routes become serverless functions.
Customises Vercel builds, redirects, environment variables, and function behaviour.
Central repo that Vercel watches; pushes trigger preview or production builds.
Tracks changes, branches, merges, and pull‑requests.
Installs JavaScript dependencies (npm install) and runs scripts (npm run dev).
Executes binaries from npm packages without a global install (e.g., npx create-next-app).
Executes the build scripts (next build, tailwindcss) and powers Vercel’s serverless functions.

column4: Superset of JavaScript with static typing
column7: Adds compile‑time type safety; optional but common in modern Next.js projects.
Core language for React, Next.js, and most tooling.
Runs Tailwind’s transformer to generate the final CSS file.
Adds vendor prefixes for broader browser compatibility.
Auto‑generated UI (/docs) that describes FastAPI endpoints.
Store secrets (e.g., DB path, API keys) without hard‑coding them.
Can run linting, tests, and custom build steps before Vercel deploys.
Useful if you want to run FastAPI locally or in a custom cloud provider instead of Vercel.
Serves the FastAPI app locally (uvicorn main:app).
Used by FastAPI to define request/response schemas (BaseModel).
Code review mechanism that triggers preview deployments on Vercel.
Each PR gets its own unique URL (<branch>—<hash>.vercel.app).
Triggered when code merges to the production branch (often main).
Generates HTML at build time; ideal for marketing pages like the Hero.
Generates HTML on each request; useful for dynamic data like metrics.
Alternative place to host simple APIs; not used here because FastAPI handles metrics.
Isolates work (e.g., feature/hero, bugfix/metrics).
Explains setup, scripts, and deployment steps for future contributors.
Enforces style and catches bugs before commit.
Guarantees that components and API endpoints work as expected.
The primary workspace for Vibe Coding. "Composer" mode writes code across multiple files simultaneously using semantic understanding.
The intelligent "brain" best suited for complex architecture, reasoning, and generating initial code plans.
Alternative IDE that maintains deep context of your codebase and user actions ("flow" state) to predict next edits.
Instantly generates production-ready UI components from text prompts to speed up the start of a project.
The "Constitution" for your project. Tells the AI your coding standards, stack, and architecture decisions to prevent drift.
A collection of re-usable components that you can copy and paste into your apps. The de-facto standard for AI-generated UIs.
The standard, clean icon set used by shadcn/ui and most modern frameworks, highly compatible with AI generators.
A production-ready motion library for React that adds professional polish and "feel" (micro-interactions) with minimal code.
Schema declaration and validation library. Crucial when AI generates code to ensure runtime data structures match TypeScript interfaces.
Replaces a custom backend team. Provides Authentication, Database, and Realtime subscriptions out of the box.
The rock-solid object-relational database system that powers Supabase. The industry standard for production data.
Allows you to call backend functions directly from frontend components (e.g., form submissions) without manually creating API routes.
Lets you interact with your database using readable TypeScript methods (db.user.findMany()) instead of writing raw SQL.
Manages fetching, caching, synchronizing and updating server state in your React applications.
A blazing fast unit test framework powered by Vite, serving as a modern, faster alternative to Jest.
Enables reliable end-to-end testing for modern web apps by automating the browser to simulate real user interactions.
A tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications (e.g., running Next.js + FastAPI + Postgres locally).
specialized authentication platform. Often used as a simpler, pre-built alternative to implementing Supabase Auth manually.
A serverless Postgres database that scales to zero. An alternative to Supabase if you only need the database layer.
A library to easily build AI-powered applications (streaming text, chat interfaces) with Next.js and React.
A fast, disk space-efficient package manager. An alternative to npm that is often preferred in modern monorepo setups.
The unstyled, accessible foundation upon which shadcn/ui is built. Handles complex logic like focus management and keyboard navigation.
A modern email sending platform for developers. Designed to be easily integrated into Next.js/React applications.
Provides serverless Redis and Kafka for caching and messaging. Useful for rate limiting and fast ephemeral data storage.
